ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.27 to rider as a Ryde voucher for unexempted detour mileage; log the RD-1 breach on driver T-2049's record (no account flag — no prior upheld route dispute).

segment_findings.reason: The GPS movement along the northward bulge (09:48:25–09:52:55) maps onto the quoted route along Ayer Rajah Expressway westbound (max deviation under 100 m); the apparent extra distance and the AYE band-4 record are map-matching residual on the optimal route, not an off-route deviation. RD-3/RD-4 (band 4 never exempts on its own; RD-4(b)).

The driver leaves the quoted route (Clementi Rd / AYE) and cuts north via Holland Ave (lateral offset ≈ 1.1–1.9 km), producing an unexempted off-route segment with ≈ 0.90–1.15 km of extra distance (net method). RD-4 not met (only band-4 speed bands, no incidents); RD-5 not met (chat consent of 09:35:25 is a lobby/pickup arrangement, not route consent; driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' is a claim, not rider consent); RD-3 not met (no rider-named stop). RD-1 → RD-2 refund.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's statement 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is contradicted by the GPS trace, which shows a lateral break of ≈ 1.1–1.9 km from the quoted route that cannot be mapped to it; a GPS reroute does not by itself satisfy RD-4's reasonable-cause test (no incident, no band 1–2 on the optimal route).

Rider's implied claim of the full ~1.4-km shortfall: only the unexempted off-route segment's extra distance (1.00 km measured) is refundable; the rest (0.63 km) is map-matching/fast-road residual on the optimal route and is not recoverable under RD-2/G1.
